staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged checkout. `sample_info.json` names metadata vulnerable commit `3055a05f0a229a11b5d8c65d42ab15ad17f3b714`, but the live prepared tree above is the exact source whose line map matches the saved ASan crash and the staged patch hunk in `blosc/frame.c`.

classification.classification_note: The public issue text labels this as a heap-buffer-overflow READ, but the staged reproduction is `AddressSanitizer: SEGV` / `wild-addr-read` in `frame_get_usermeta()`. The underlying flaw is still a missing bounds check before a read from attacker-controlled frame storage.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42489773 (c-blosc2): Heap-buffer-overflow READ {*} found by fuzz target decompress_frame_fuzzer [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42489773
bug_description.normalized: Passing the exact staged 91-byte `poc` to `decompress_frame_fuzzer` makes `blosc2_schunk_open_sframe()` call `blosc2_frame_from_sframe(sframe, len, false)`, so the project parses the attacker buffer as an in-memory frame without copying it. The serialized `frame_len` field matches the input size, so the frame is accepted and `frame->sdata` aliases the attacker bytes. `blosc2_schunk_open_sframe()` then calls `blosc2_frame_to_schunk(frame, false)`. In that function, the first `get_header_info()` execution parses a huge positive `nbytes` and `chunksize = 0x20202020`, so `nchunks` truncates to the nonzero value `2`; with caller-supplied `copy = false`, `if (!copy || nchunks == 0)` takes the `!copy` fast path. After the empty-metalayer parse succeeds, `frame_get_usermeta()` re-executes `get_header_info()` and materializes its own local `header_len = 0x20202020`, `frame_len = 91`, and `cbytes = 0`. `get_trailer_offset()` therefore returns that local `header_len` as `trailer_offset`. Vulnerable `frame_get_usermeta()` checks only `trailer_offset < 0` instead of bounding `trailer_offset + FRAME_TRAILER_USERMETA_LEN_OFFSET` against its local `frame_len`, so the positive out-of-range offset survives and line 928 reads four bytes from `frame->sdata + 0x20202020 + 3`, producing the saved ASan wild-address read. The staged patch closes this by checking `trailer_offset + FRAME_TRAILER_USERMETA_LEN_OFFSET > frame_len` before the read.

source.description: First project-code statement on the vulnerable path that parses attacker-controlled frame metadata from the fuzz buffer.
source.value_from: In the staged 91-byte `poc`, bytes 16-23 are `00 00 00 00 00 00 00 5b`, so this statement materializes `frame_len = 91`, matching the full input size and keeping the buffer on the in-memory frame path.

root_cause.description: After `frame_get_usermeta()` re-executes `get_header_info()`, the function checks only `trailer_offset < 0` and never enforces that `trailer_offset + FRAME_TRAILER_USERMETA_LEN_OFFSET` stays within its local `frame_len`. On the witness, the reparsed `trailer_offset` is the attacker-controlled `header_len` value `0x20202020`, so the positive out-of-range offset reaches the read.
root_cause.note: The staged patch inserts this missing upper-bound guard immediately after the negative-offset test and returns `-1` when it fails.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer sink. After the second local parse in `frame_get_usermeta()`, the parser reads the 4-byte usermeta length from a pointer computed with the unchecked positive `trailer_offset`, so it dereferences far beyond the 91-byte attacker buffer.
sink.note: Stage 01's saved ASan trace reports the crash at `blosc/frame.c:928` with address `0x6080202020c3` and stack `frame_get_usermeta -> blosc2_frame_to_schunk -> blosc2_schunk_open_sframe`.

tainted_value_origin.description: This `swap_store` site materializes the attacker-controlled header-length field. The `frame_get_usermeta()` execution of the same statement later feeds the unchecked trailer offset when `cbytes == 0`.
tainted_value_origin.value_from: The staged `poc` stores `0x20 0x20 0x20 0x20` at bytes 11-14, so `header_len` becomes `0x20202020` (`538976288`).

parser_admitted.description: After the `copy=false` fast path jumps to `out:`, the witness still passes `frame_get_metalayers()`: bytes 86-88 are `0xde 0x00 0x00`, so the fixmap marker is accepted and `nmetalayers` is zero. That return-path admission is what allows control to reach `frame_get_usermeta()`.

evidence_limitations: The prepared checkout Stage 01 executed is `474ebf151be847186e6bc2c1381a8f7d4beff4dd`, while metadata lists vulnerable commit `3055a05f0a229a11b5d8c65d42ab15ad17f3b714`; this GT is grounded in the exact staged source tree that reproduced and whose line map matches the saved crash.

`run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to false, so Stage 02 did not instrument. The chain is closed entirely from the staged source, patch, saved ASan trace, reproduction report, and direct inspection of the staged `poc` bytes.
Stage 02 does not execute the fixed tree, so `sanitizer_ground_truth.patch_resolves` remains false even though the staged patch directly adds the missing guard.

coarse_trace.summary: The harness passes the attacker-controlled buffer directly to `blosc2_schunk_open_sframe()` as an in-memory serialized frame.
The open helper forwards the attacker buffer into `blosc2_frame_from_sframe(..., false)`, so the accepted frame keeps a no-copy alias to the witness bytes.

`blosc2_schunk_open_sframe()` then calls `blosc2_frame_to_schunk(frame, false)`; the first `get_header_info()` parses malformed size fields, computes nonzero `nchunks`, and the caller's `copy=false` makes the `!copy` fast path reach `frame_get_usermeta()` after the empty-metalayer parse succeeds.

Inside `frame_get_usermeta()`, a second `get_header_info()` reparses local `header_len = 0x20202020`, `frame_len = 91`, and `cbytes = 0`; `get_trailer_offset()` returns the unchecked positive header length, and the line-928 `memcpy()` overreads attacker buffer memory and crashes.

fine_trace.note: The project open helper forwards the attacker buffer and its 91-byte length into `blosc2_frame_from_sframe()` with `copy = false`, fixing the no-copy policy that later keeps `frame->sdata` aliased to the witness bytes.
Source. With `len = 91` (at least `FRAME_HEADER_MINLEN`), the in-memory frame parser reads bytes 16-23 of the attacker buffer as the serialized frame length and materializes `frame_len = 91`.
The size-equality check is the admission gate for this path. Because the same call supplied `len = 91`, the parsed `frame_len` matches and the function does not return `NULL`.
Because the caller chose `copy = false` at step 1, the `if (copy)` branch is skipped and the returned frame keeps a direct alias to the attacker buffer instead of copying it.
The same open helper immediately converts the parsed frame with a second literal `false`, fixing `copy = false` for `blosc2_frame_to_schunk()` and its fast-path predicate.

In the first `get_header_info()` call from `blosc2_frame_to_schunk()`, bytes 30-37 decode to the huge positive `nbytes = 0x202020202020ff20`, providing the numerator for the later `nchunks` computation.
The same first `get_header_info()` call decodes bytes 53-56 as `chunksize = 0x20202020` (`538976288`), providing the divisor for the later `nchunks` computation.

Because both parsed sizes are positive, this block computes nonzero `nchunks` for the witness: the quotient `0x100000001` truncates to `1` as `int32_t`, and the positive remainder increments it to `2`.

The fast-path predicate is satisfied, but not by the `nchunks == 0` arm. Step 5 supplied `copy = false`, and step 8 already made `nchunks = 2`, so `!copy` is the arm that jumps directly to `out:` and bypasses chunk/offset copying.

After the `!copy` fast path and the empty-metalayer checkpoint, `frame_get_usermeta()` re-executes `get_header_info()` on the same aliased buffer and materializes its own local `header_len = 0x20202020` from bytes 11-14.
The same second `get_header_info()` call materializes local `frame_len = 91` inside `frame_get_usermeta()`. This is the exact bound the missing upper-bound guard should use.
The same second `get_header_info()` call materializes local `cbytes = 0` inside `frame_get_usermeta()`, selecting the zero-chunk trailer-offset branch.
Because the second parse produced local `cbytes == 0`, `get_trailer_offset()` returns that same local `header_len` unchanged, so `frame_get_usermeta()` receives `trailer_offset = 0x20202020`.

Root cause. After reparsing `frame_len = 91`, the function still checks only `trailer_offset < 0`. The witness's `trailer_offset` is the large positive value `0x20202020`, so this check falls through even though `trailer_offset + FRAME_TRAILER_USERMETA_LEN_OFFSET` already exceeds `frame_len`.

Sink. The parser reads four bytes from `frame->sdata + 0x20202020 + 3`, far beyond the 91-byte attacker buffer aliased at step 4. Stage 01's ASan trace records the resulting fault at `blosc/frame.c:928` as `SEGV` / `wild-addr-read` with crash address `0x6080202020c3`.

poc.trigger: Pass the exact staged 91-byte `poc` to `decompress_frame_fuzzer`; the project keeps the buffer aliased with `copy = false`, the first `get_header_info()` in `blosc2_frame_to_schunk()` computes nonzero `nchunks`, and the second `get_header_info()` in `frame_get_usermeta()` reparses `header_len = 0x20202020`, `frame_len = 91`, and `cbytes = 0`, so the unchecked trailer-offset read on line 928 overreaches the buffer.

format.name: serialized blosc2 in-memory frame
format.contract: The verified witness is the exact staged 91-byte buffer exercised through `decompress_frame_fuzzer`, which in turn calls `blosc2_schunk_open_sframe()` with `copy = false`. In that exact buffer, bytes 16-23 encode `frame_len = 91` so the in-memory frame is admitted, bytes 30-37 and 53-56 make the first `get_header_info()` compute nonzero `nchunks` (`2` on the staged build), bytes 86-88 encode an empty metalayer index (`de 00 00`), and bytes 11-14 plus 39-46 make the later `frame_get_usermeta()` reparse `header_len = 0x20202020` and `cbytes = 0`. Those exact witness facts are what let `get_trailer_offset()` return the header length as a positive out-of-range `trailer_offset` before the line-928 read.
